scenes.title: Delivery Semantics
scenes.subtitle: At-most-once, at-least-once, and exactly-once
scenes.narration: Delivery semantics describe the guarantee Kafka gives about whether a message may be lost, duplicated, or delivered exactly once.

scenes.title: The Three Guarantees
bullets: At-most-once: may lose messages, never duplicates
Exactly-once: no loss and no duplicates
The guarantee depends on producer and consumer config
scenes.narration: At-most-once delivery may lose messages but never duplicates them, which suits metrics where the odd gap is tolerable. At-least-once never loses a message but may deliver it more than once, making it the common default. Exactly-once delivers each message once and only once, at the cost of extra coordination. Which guarantee you get depends on how both the producer and consumer are configured.

scenes.title: Why Duplicates Happen
steps: Ack is lost on the network
scenes.narration: Duplicates arise from retries. A producer sends a message and the broker successfully writes it. But the acknowledgement is lost on the network before it reaches the producer. Believing the send failed, the producer retries, and the broker writes a second copy. Idempotent producers solve this by tagging each message so the broker can discard the duplicate.

scenes.title: At-Least-Once vs Exactly-Once
scenes.narration: For at-least-once, you enable producer retries and have the consumer commit its offset only after processing succeeds, then make downstream logic tolerate duplicates. For exactly-once, you combine an idempotent producer with transactions that atomically write records and commit offsets, while consumers use the read-committed isolation level. Exactly-once is powerful but adds latency and complexity, so use it only where correctness demands it.

scenes.title: Configuring the Guarantee
scenes.code:
# At-least-once with idempotence (no duplicates from retries)
producer = Producer({
    'bootstrap.servers': 'localhost:9092',
    'enable.idempotence': True,
    'acks': 'all',
    'retries': 5,
})

# Consumer commits AFTER processing
for msg in poll_loop():
    process(msg)      # do the work first
    consumer.commit(msg)  # then record progress
scenes.narration: Here idempotence, acks all, and retries give the producer safe at-least-once behavior with no duplicates from retries. On the consumer side, the order matters: process the message first, then commit the offset. If you committed before processing and then crashed, you would lose the message, sliding toward at-most-once. Doing the work first keeps you safely at at-least-once.

scenes.text: At-least-once with idempotent, deduplicated processing covers most needs. Reserve full exactly-once transactions for money-movement and similar correctness-critical flows.
scenes.narration: As a rule of thumb, at-least-once combined with idempotent, deduplicated processing covers most needs. Reserve full exactly-once transactions for money movement and other correctness-critical flows.
